subject: Pilot corridor: dataset exchange & acceptance journey
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <sam@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot corridor: dataset exchange & acceptance journey

Hi Samantha —

Great speaking yesterday. As discussed, we want to put a short mutual action plan (MAP) in place so the Atlas pilot can get the evaluation assets we need, and Atlas has a repeatable acceptance path for the retail use cases. High level proposal below; please confirm or propose changes.

What Redwood will deliver to Atlas:
- A prompt pack (example templates + negative examples) for the retail category extraction task.
- A curated test case subset (approx. 2k lines) representing real storefront edge cases.
- One sandbox deployment of the chosen model variant for convenience during evaluation.

What Atlas will provide to Redwood:
- Secure transfer of anonymized product metadata (schema attached) under the one-way usage constraints below.
- Acceptance criteria feedback within the agreed windows.

Key usage constraints (Atlas requests):
- Assets are licensed for pilot evaluation only; no production serving, derivative data resell, or persistence beyond the pilot.
- Redwood to destroy local copies 30 days after pilot close unless a written extension is agreed.

Proposed milestones / close timeline:
1) Asset exchange window: May 14–16 — Atlas deposits eval assets in the agreed SFTP + sends sample manifest.
2) Ingest & sanity checks (Redwood): May 17–20 — schema verification, data QC, promptpack import.
3) First-pass eval and sync call: May 23 — deliver initial metrics and failure-mode examples.
4) Acceptance window & tweaks: May 24–30 — iterations and signoff.
5) Pilot close + destruction confirmation: by Jun 30 (unless extended).

Attachments: atlas_eval_promptpack_v1.zip (prompt templates), redwood_map_draft_20250512.pdf (proposed MAP doc).

Next step: if the timeline looks good, Marissa will send a short transfer checklist + SFTP credentials template and Ben will scope the ingest QA.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Liu <sam@atlasretail.com>

Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 12:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot corridor: dataset exchange & acceptance journey

Thanks Karthik — this reads well and aligns with what I communicated internally. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 2k testcases should exclude any PII; we'll run a scrub prior to transfer.
- Procurement needs the MAP doc with a statement on retention and destruction for compliance sign-off. Can you switch the "30 days" phrasing to "30 calendar days after formal written close"?
- We would like a lighter anonymized sample by May 14 so our data governance team can validate the scrub.

Small ask on the licensing text: Atlas requests that Redwood confirms in writing that the pilot assets will not be used to further train any public-facing models or published externally. If you accept, we can proceed to share SFTP details and initiate the exchange.

Sam
Samantha Liu
Director, Product Analytics
Atlas Retail Solutions

Hi Sam —

Quick follow-up from Redwood operations: happy to reword the retention clause to "30 calendar days after formal written close" — I'll update the MAP draft. On the training concern: Redwood will not use the pilot assets to further train or fine-tune any public models or publish the raw assets. We can add a short non-training covenant to the MAP and a simple attestation for your procurement team.

Logistics / checklist items I'm putting together for the transfer (we'll send as a one-page checklist):
- Deliver anonymized sample (<= 100 rows) by Thu May 14 — data governance sign-off.
- Full deposit to SFTP (sftp.atlasretail.com:/incoming/redwood-atlas-pilot) May 14–16.
- File manifest: atlas_testcases_subset.csv + metadata schema + checksum file.
- Redwood will run intake scripts and return a QC report within 48 business hours of deposit.

Ben — I'll need a short estimate for the ingest/QC work (hours + any special handling) so I can confirm the May 17 start.

Sam — can you confirm procurement contact is okay with the attestation language? If yes, we'll attach the updated MAP PDF and the checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa

Hi all —

Estimate for the ingest + QC: 1 engineer (4 hours) for intake and schema validation; 1 engineer (8 hours) to run full checks and produce the QC report and failure-mode examples. If Atlas needs additional custom parsing for storefront categories (rare formats), add a 6–10 hour buffer. Total conservative estimate: 18 engineer-hours.

I confirmed the SFTP path and checked permissions; Sam, your team should be able to deposit the sample tomorrow. We'll begin ingest on May 17 as planned provided the sample and manifest look good.

I've attached a short checklist and the sample manifest template.
